messages:
maggie: FYI — after the eu keywrap rotation last night we started seeing a small spike in proxy -> model-svc TLS handshake failures. hitting session ticket unwrap errors in the proxy logs. anyone seen this before?
rajesh: can you paste a couple of trace lines? which proxies/regions?
maggie: eu-west cluster, proxy pool p-eu-01. here's the relevant extract from the proxy logs: ```Mar 20 01:14:03 proxy p-eu-01 ssl_handshake: ticket_unwrap_failed key_id=projects/rdw/keyrings/keystore/cryptoKeys/rtk/cryptoKeyVersions/3 error=INVALID_CREDENTIALS SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL at accept()```
sylvie: seeing 502 spikes on the dashboard at ~01:15-01:20 UTC, ~6% of requests. oncall flagged it.
dave: quick theory: we enabled session tickets for perf and tickets are encrypted with a key-wrapping key bound to a KMS key version. if the rotator retired v3 immediately, proxies can't unwrap older tickets. short-term mitigation is to disable session ticket resume on proxies so clients do full TLS handshake until tickets expire.
rajesh: can confirm the rotation job retired version v3 — but our rotator should have left older versions accessible for 72h. checking rotator logs and KMS audit now.
maggie: also worried about RBAC: did the rotator change principal used for unwraps? if the proxy instances lost decrypt/unwrap permission for keyversions we might see this. need KMS audit entries listing which identity attempted Unwrap and whether it failed.
dave: exact quick checks: 1) query KMS audit for UnwrapKey/Decrypt events for key versions around 01:10-01:20 UTC, filter by principal p-eu-01 or service account used by proxies. 2) check rotator job logs for retire timing and whether it set state=disabled vs destroyed. sample queries: ```gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricDecrypt" AND timestamp>="2026-03-20T01:00:00Z"' --limit 50``` or for AWS CloudTrail: ```aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2026-03-20T01:00:00 --end-time 2026-03-20T01:30```
sylvie: if we flip the session-ticket flag it should be a quick config change no deploy; proxies read FEATURE_DISABLE_SESSION_TICKETS env at reload. oncall can toggle and watch error rate. threshold: if errors drop <1% in 10m we can keep it off while we investigate.
rajesh: I pulled rotator logs: "KeyWrapRotation job completed 2026-03-20T01:12Z, key-version v3 -> retired". rotator output shows it removed 'unwrap' role from the service account used by older proxies as part of tidy-up — that looks like an accidental RBAC prune.
maggie: oh — so rotator removed principal binding too aggressively. we need two immediate things: 1) restore unwrap permissions to the proxy service account for the retired v3 until tickets TTL passes, 2) revert rotator RBAC change and update playbook.
dave: mitigation steps: - restore IAM binding: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding rtk --member=serviceAccount:proxy-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter --keyring=keystore` - re-enable key-version retirement policy to wait X hours after rotate - set proxies to not rely on session tickets across rotations.
maggie: vuln triage note: severity is low — this is availability / config drift, not key compromise. but it's a config management vuln: rotator should never remove unwrap perms for still-in-use keyversions. mark as P2 and add to security backlog.
sylvie: oncall toggled FEATURE_DISABLE_SESSION_TICKETS=1 on p-eu-01 now (rollout started). will report metrics in 5m.
kms-bot: [automated] KeyWrapRotation job 2026-03-20T01:12Z completed. rotated current key -> v4, retired v3 at 2026-03-20T01:12:10Z. rotator-run id=kwr-2026-03-20-1; diff: removed IAM binding proxy-sa from keyversion v3.
rajesh: I'm submitting an incident ticket (INC-2026-187) to track RBAC rollback, audit queries, and playbook updates. assigning to maggie/dave.
maggie: thanks — once proxies are stable we'll update the rotator to (a) not remove bindings for N hours and (b) emit an audit event pinned to the rotation run with affected principals. also add an automated canary that fails rotation if proxy unwrap error rate > 0.5% within 30m.
dave: add to checklist: ensure audit logging of Unwrap/Decrypt includes principal and keyversion in plaintext fields (avoid only aggregated logs). retrospective: look for similar rotations in apac/us regions last quarter.
sylvie: 5m check: error rate down to 0.9% after flag flip, still trending down. continuing watch.
maggie: thanks all. follow-ups: create PR for rotator RBAC safeguard, update runbook with rollback commands, and query KMS audit for any failed unwraps to confirm no widespread impact.
